title: North Star 1:1 microagenda & unblock plan
content:
Goal: 30-minute focused 1:1 covering project blockers, short-term growth step, and a single prioritized outcome for next week. Keep actionable; leave with concrete next steps (owner + date).

Meeting structure (30m total)
- 0-3m: Quick mood check + red/amber/green on workload
- 3-10m: Top blocker deep dive (ENG-4821) — decide who pairs with whom and timeline
- 10-17m: Career pulse & skill pick for the sprint (focus: async API design reviews)
- 17-25m: Metrics review + runway risks (latency p50/p95, CS feedback)
- 25-30m: Concrete commitments & blockers to surface to SRE/product

Prep notes to self (things to ask / watch for)
- Is the rollout hesitation due to testing infra or docs? (probe: last trial log timestamps)
- Check whether Diego's benchmark artifacts were uploaded — if not, get ETA
- Ask about onboarding friction for new ICs reviewing model variants — one example story
- Career: offer a small stretch project (lead a proposal for async review process)
- Wellbeing: catch any signs of burnout (long weekend schedule, late-night commits)

Top Blocker (ENG-4821) — KV cache invalidation causing tail-latency spikes
- Current hypothesis: race condition when cache purge and concurrent requests trigger cold-fill path repeatedly
- Evidence: p99 increases correlate with cache-purge cron at hh:45; logs show multiple identical cold-fill traces
- Options to resolve (weigh quick vs robust):
  1) Quick patch: add a short global lock around cache-populate (low effort, risk of small throughput hit)
  2) Medium: dedupe cold-fill in-flight requests with request coalescing by key (more work, reduces duplicates)
  3) Long-term: rework cache eviction + TTL to avoid synchronous purges on high-traffic keys
- My recommended path: go with option 1 as an immediate mitigation, schedule option 2 for next sprint with Diego + SRE pairing

Action items from blocker discussion (to assign in meeting)
- Elena: open a focused PR with the global lock proof-of-concept, include benchmark script and a short risk note — due 2026-03-10
- Diego: run the coalescing perf experiment branch and share results in PR comments — due 2026-03-12
- Ravi: add targeted alert for repeated cold-fill identity within 1m window (Pager duty FYI) — due 2026-03-09

Metrics snapshot to review (bring up live dashboard)
- p50 latency: 28ms (target <=30ms)
- p95 latency: 240ms (target <=200ms) — tail drift concerns
- error rate: 0.12% (spikes near purge window)
- rollout success rate (canary): 97% last 24h

Career / growth micro-commit (10–15m discussion)
- Suggestion: take ownership of the async API review proposal and shepherd it through design review
  - Deliverable: one-page design sketch + pro/con table + example call flow
  - Why: builds API design cred, cross-team exposure, and a visible leadership step
- Offer: I will pair with them on the first draft and do a dry-run in our sync with Product
- Commitment: draft due 2026-03-22, dry-run 2026-03-25

Check-ins & follow-ups to schedule
- Quick 20m follow-up next week to validate lock PR impact on tail latency (target week of 2026-03-15)
- Sync with SRE/infra for coalescing design review (30m) — propose 2026-03-16
- Add item to team retro to discuss cache-purge cadence and visibility (owner: Maya)

Notes-to-self: phrasing and coaching prompts
- If they push back on 'locking' as degrading throughput, acknowledge concern and reframe as a temporary safemode while we build a cleaner coalescing solution
- Encourage ownership language: "Would you be willing to own the async review proposal?" rather than "Can you do this?"
- If signs of bandwidth stress: help reprioritize (remove a nonessential task this sprint)

Post-meeting quick checklist (what I'll do immediately after 1:1)
- Send short recap thread in DM with explicit action items and deadlines (copy Ravi/Maya as needed)
- Open ENG-4821 subtask for PR + benchmark artifacts, tag Diego and Ravi
- Create quick dashboard snapshot and pin to the meeting note (so we can see before follow-up)

Possible risks to call out during the meeting
- If global lock introduces unexpected throughput regression, be ready to roll back and toggle via feature flag
- Communicate to Product if canary success dips below 95% during mitigation window

Back-pocket talking points (if time runs short)
- "What's the one risk you'd like me to remove from your plate this sprint?"
- "What would success look like for you in 2 weeks?"

End state for next 1:1 (what we should have accomplished)
- Lock PR merged and no tail-latency regression in 48h after deploy OR rollback plan executed
- Design sketch for async API review drafted and one stakeholder dry-run scheduled
- Clear owner for cache coalescing work and SRE alignment scheduled

Rough commit list (for my calendar and follow-up)
- 2026-03-09: Ravi alert changes + Pager note done
- 2026-03-10: Elena PR + benchmark scripts opened (link in comments)
- 2026-03-12: Diego experiment results posted
- 2026-03-15: short follow-up 20m 1:1 to validate mitigation
- 2026-03-22: async API proposal draft due

Random scratch / things to paste in meeting:
- Quick snippet to share: "Observed p99 jump aligns with cache purge at HH:45 — repeating cold-fill traces. Proposed temporary global lock to reduce duplicate cold-fill warms by >90% in local sim."
- Quick ask to SRE: "Can we add a per-key duplication metric (count of concurrent cold-fill starts) to the realtime dashboard?"

End.
